step1_analysis.description: A single PMOS transistor connected between VDD and GND, controlled by the VSUM node. It acts as a voltage-controlled shunt resistor or current sink, likely used for pulse biasing or as a dummy load.

paper_reference.title: A Temperature-to-Digital Converter for a MEMSBased Programmable Oscillator with Better Than ±0.5ppm Frequency Stability

I_on.description: Maximum shunt current when VSUM is 0V

sky130_expected.reasoning: Calculated using the square law model with channel length modulation for SKY130 PMOS at 1.8V.

Vth_vsum.description: Input voltage VSUM at which the PMOS turns on (Id = 1uA)

sky130_expected.reasoning: Threshold voltage of the PMOS relative to the VDD supply.
Calculated from the maximum current and overdrive voltage.

step3_testbench.description: DC sweep of VSUM to characterize the PMOS shunt transistor's current, threshold, and transconductance.
step3_testbench.spice:
* PMOS Shunt Characterization
.lib "${SKY130_PDK}" tt

.param W_xm1=5u L_xm1=0.5u

XM1 GND VSUM VDD VDD sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 l={L_xm1} w={W_xm1}

VVDD VDD 0 1.8
VVSUM VSUM 0 1.8

.control
  dc VVSUM 0 1.8 0.01
  let id = -i(VVDD)
  let gm = -deriv(id)
  
  meas dc I_on find id at=0
  meas dc Vth_vsum when id=1u
  meas dc gm_max max gm
  
  print I_on Vth_vsum gm_max
  quit
.endc
.end
